nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $M$ be a matching subgraph of $G$, so that every vertex of $M$ is incident to exactly one edge of $M$. Then $M$ has the maximum number of edges among all matching subgraphs of $G$ if and only if there is no $M$-augmenting path: a path in $G$ of positive length between two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$, neither of which is a vertex of $M$, whose consecutive…
nodes.title: Berge's lemma for matching subgraphs

nodes.summary: A matching $M$ of a simple graph on a finite vertex set is maximum if and only if no walk is $M$-augmenting. This restates Berge's lemma with the named predicate.
nodes.title: Berge's lemma with augmenting walks

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $M$ be a matching of $G$, that is, a finite set of edges of $G$ no two distinct members of which share a vertex. Then $M$ has maximum cardinality among all matchings of $G$ if and only if there is no $M$-augmenting path: a path in $G$ of positive length between two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$, neither of which lies on an edge of $M$, whose consecutive edges…
nodes.title: Berge's lemma

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be matchings of a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set. Then there are $|N| - |M|$ pairwise vertex-disjoint $M$-augmenting walks whose edges all lie in the symmetric difference $M \oplus N$. Hopcroft and Karp state it for $|N| > |M|$; for $|N| \le |M|$ the truncated difference is $0$ and the statement is empty.
nodes.title: Disjoint augmenting paths in a symmetric difference (Hopcroft–Karp, Theorem 1)

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be matchings of a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set with $r = |M| < |N|$. Then some $M$-augmenting walk has length at most $2 \lfloor r / (|N| - r) \rfloor + 1$.
nodes.title: A short augmenting path exists (Hopcroft–Karp, Corollary 2)

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite set of edges of a simple graph $G$, in practice a matching. A walk $p$ from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ is *$M$-augmenting* if $u \ne v$, $p$ has positive length and no repeated vertex, neither $u$ nor $v$ lies on an edge of $M$, and consecutive edges of $p$ alternate between edges in $M$ and edges not in $M$. Since the endpoints are not covered by $M$, the first and last edges are not in $M$, so $p$ has…
nodes.title: Augmenting path

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matching of a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, $p$ a shortest $M$-augmenting walk, and $q$ a walk that is augmenting for the matching $M \oplus E(p)$. Then $|q| \ge |p| + |E(p) \cap E(q)|$, lengths counting edges.
nodes.title: Augmenting after a shortest augmentation (Hopcroft–Karp, Theorem 2)

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matching of a simple graph $G$ and $p$ an $M$-augmenting walk. Then the symmetric difference $M \oplus E(p)$ of $M$ with the edge set of $p$ is a matching of $G$ with $|M| + 1$ edges.
nodes.title: Augmenting along a path (Hopcroft–Karp, Lemma 1)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
